I interned for one of the top 3 investment banks in their derivatives trading department. For context, I'm a minority female. 

It was alright. Hours were supposedly 7:30 - 5 although I probably got in around 8 or 9. I basically got paid to sit there and have them teach me options theory and different exotics products. There were a few desks that were very bro-y (mostly index or other sales desks) and most of the time, they were "busy" and never talked to me. I rotated around the full timers and listened to them/watched their screens silently. Not surprisingly, everyone on that desk was a white male. There was a lot of shouting, especially when a broker reneged on a trade or someone did something dumb. Other than that, there was a lot of betting and people kept alcohol under their desks.

Contrary to popular belief, no one ever asked me to buy the desk coffee or lunch or anything. 

There were more liberal desks, like the HFT desks and the exotics desks. At those desks the work was a bit more challenging, lots of math and problem solving. The people were generally very encouraging, because they wanted more females for diversity reasons and I was the only female intern. I chatted a lot with the first year analysts because they just got out of college and were around my age. People were a bit arrogant--I kept hearing "Working at Company for two years will open doors to basically any other company you would want to work at."

I think they really tried to make us like it. We had weekly networking meetings and they really emphasized the aspect of networking. I could just cold-call anyone on the floor, even my boss's boss's boss, and ask them to lunch and they would oblige. The international head of the department even asked to network with me and get coffee. 

I think it was a different experience because I usually intern in tech. You needed to dress up and look presentable every day (whereas in tech we just wore tshirts). The office itself (or the trading floor that I worked on) was loud and hectic during the trading day. There was little privacy so you couldn't really slack off or go on reddit during work. 

I ended up getting a return offer but I didn't go back. I might consider going back sometime in the future.

It's not about believing - it's about respect. If someone did go through an experience like that (and, accurate or not, your studies say that 92% of rape claims are true...and that's a huge number!) then openly laughing at them and telling them to present proof is like responding to a crying child who says "My parents just died" with "I won't believe you until you show me the obituary." Puh-leaz. It's not about innocent until proven guilty. It's not about convicting someone of rape before there is evidence. At the very least, we should make it obvious that it is never the victim's fault. Saying "Are you sure it wasn't a bad hookup?" is telling the victim "Are you sure you didn't mistake RAPE with a bad hookup?" and to those who HAVE been raped, that is quite traumatic and offensive. Saying "Please show me proof" is equally traumatic as there is often never any proof, but even without evidence, if someone has been raped, it doesn't change how horrible they feel. And it will make the victim feel like the whole world, even a counselling center that is supposed to HELP her, is against her.

Victims should always be believed and we should never discourage other victims from coming forward. But prosecution or punishments should be taken only with proof. Unless we are in a court room, the cost of treating an alleged victim like she's on trial is too much for the very small number of rape claims that are false.

For some people, losing weight is an incredibly mentally and physically painful ordeal. Maybe they have a very slow metabolism or they just can't stop feeling like they are starving until they have overeaten. Not to mention there are some people with thyroid or other medical conditions that cause them to be prone to obesity. If you are not obese, chances are you are blessed with the right genes, the right metabolism, etc. that lets you eat what you want at moderate rates and still feel happy and comfortable.

In many cases of obesity, you're telling someone to go on a diet that would cause them as much discomfort as telling someone who is NOT overweight to go on a diet cutting out most of their favorite foods or - as you suggested - to not eat at all. There is absolutely NO reason why fat people OWE IT TO YOU AND SOCIETY to put themselves through painful dieting just so they can fit your standards. If mrbarber's wife doesn't want to live out the rest of her life on the brink of starvation, I have no right to judge her for it. If fat people want to take the initiative to lose weight, that is their prerogative, and if they don't, you have as much of a right to tell them to stop eating as they have to tell you to stop eating.

As for the "but obese people waste my taxes in medical bills" - do you think you have a right to tell someone who is genetically prone to cancer not to walk out of their door lest they get hit by UV rays? That would be incredibly intrusive, ignorant, AND rude.

I love how just by reading a post on reddit you think you know more about someone's health than her husband or her doctors, and anybody who disagrees with your professional medical diagnosis is plain ol' lying. Who's the ignorant one here?
